about.title: About Churchy
about.intro: Churchy brings parishes and their faithful closer together through digital tools.
about.whyText: Preparing a Mass takes time, and parish information is often scattered: printed sheets, notice boards, messages. Churchy brings it all together in one place, easy for the parish to publish and easy for the faithful to read.
about.missionText: To let every parish publish its Masses, celebration sheets, announcements and activities, and every member of the faithful find them before coming.
about.question: A question? <link>Write to us</link>.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Welcome to Churchy. These terms explain what the service lets you do, what you can expect from it and what we expect from you. Please read them before creating an account.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Churchy is an online service that lets parishes prepare their celebrations (order of service, hymns, psalms, readings), publish their Masses, announcements and activities, and lets worshippers and visitors read them freely.
These terms of use (“Terms”) apply to anyone using the site, whether just browsing or holding an account. By using the site, you accept these Terms.

sections.title: Definitions
items: “Visitor”: anyone who browses the public site without signing in.
“User”: anyone holding an account.
“Parish”: the community represented on Churchy by a public page and a management area.
“Parish administrator”: the user who manages the parish, its members and their roles.
“Content”: all texts, images, times, announcements, celebration descriptions, hymns, psalms and readings published or entered on the service.

sections.title: Access to the service
paragraphs: Browsing the public site (finding a parish, Mass times, announcements, activities, calendar) is free and needs no account. It is available in French and English.

Management features require an account. Your internet connection costs (data plan, equipment) are your own. The service is designed to work on phones, tablets and computers, including over a slow connection.

sections.title: Accounts and roles
paragraphs: To create an account you provide a valid email address, your last name, first name and a password. You agree to give accurate information and keep it up to date. Your email address must be confirmed using the link we send you.

You alone are responsible for keeping your password confidential and for how your account is used. Do not share it; tell us without delay if you think it has been compromised. A member’s role in a parish determines what they can do:
items: Administrator: manages the parish, its public information, its members and their roles;
Preparer: prepares and publishes celebrations, announcements and activities;
Reader: views the parish’s preparations, including unpublished ones;
Viewer: views the parish’s preparations, read-only.

sections.title: The role of the parish and its administrators
paragraphs: Churchy provides the tool; each parish decides what it publishes and who may act on it. A parish administrator declares having the standing to represent it (parish priest, secretariat, pastoral team or authorised person) and carefully chooses the people given a role.

Churchy does not check each person’s authority over their parish; if people claiming the same parish dispute it, we may freeze changes to the page until the competent church authority confirms who is in charge.

sections.title: Content published by parishes
paragraphs: Each parish is responsible for the content it enters or publishes, for its accuracy and for the rights attached to it. Content you publish must be lawful, respectful of others and consistent with the mission of a religious community.

You grant us, for as long as you use the service, a non-exclusive, free right to host, display and reproduce that content only as far as needed to run Churchy (display on the public page, preview when a link is shared, backups). You keep your rights.

sections.title: Liturgical texts, hymns and copyright
paragraphs: Churchy does not supply liturgical texts, scores or hymn lyrics. You enter whatever you wish to keep yourself. Some liturgical texts, translations, hymns, psalms, scores and images are protected by copyright or neighbouring rights.

By publishing such content you warrant that you hold the necessary rights or permissions (publisher, author, rights society, parish licence). Churchy does not check these rights and cannot answer for them. The parish also remains solely responsible for the liturgical conformity of its preparations.

sections.title: Accuracy of public information
paragraphs: Times, places, cancellations and announcements shown on a parish page are supplied by that parish. Times are shown in the parish’s time zone. Although we do our best to keep the display reliable, for essential information (special time, funeral, wedding) we advise you to check directly with the parish.
A cancelled date stays visible as such, with its public reason, so that worshippers do not travel for nothing.

sections.title: Prohibited uses
paragraphs: It is forbidden, in particular, to:
items: publish unlawful, defamatory, abusive, discriminatory or hateful content, or content inciting violence;
impersonate a person, a parish or a religious authority;
publish other people’s personal data (phone, address, photograph) without their consent;
use the service for commercial or advertising purposes unrelated to parish life, or for partisan political purposes;
attempt to access other users’ accounts or data, bypass the site’s protections, disrupt its operation or query it in a massive automated way;
introduce malicious code into a text, image or form.

sections.title: Moderation, suspension and deletion
paragraphs: We may remove content that clearly breaches these Terms or the law, or suspend an account or a page, notably after a report. We try to warn the person concerned and let them explain, except in an emergency or where the law requires otherwise. You can report content through the Contact page.

sections.title: Churchy’s intellectual property
paragraphs: The Churchy name, logo, visual identity, code, interface texts and the way the service is organised are protected. They may not be copied, modified or reused without written permission, beyond the normal use of the service.

sections.title: Personal data
paragraphs: How your data is processed is described in the privacy policy, which forms part of these Terms. A parish’s public information (name, address, contacts, times) is meant to be seen by everyone; administrators must only include contact details they are entitled to publish.

sections.title: Availability of the service
paragraphs: We strive to keep the service available at all times, but it may be interrupted for maintenance, updates or outages, without entitling anyone to compensation. We cannot guarantee that no data will ever be lost: keep your own copy of important texts.

sections.title: Liability
paragraphs: The service is provided “as is”. Within the limits allowed by law, Churchy cannot be held liable for:
items: content published by parishes and users, or any infringement of third-party rights it may cause;
harm resulting from inaccurate or outdated information or temporary unavailability (for example a missed Mass because of a wrong time);
fraudulent use of an account whose password was not kept safe;
interruptions linked to the internet, electricity or phone networks, or indirect damage.
after: Nothing in these Terms excludes liability that cannot lawfully be excluded.

sections.title: Closing your account
paragraphs: You may stop using the service at any time and ask for your account to be deleted through the Contact page. We may close an inactive account or one that breaches the Terms. Deleting an account does not erase a parish’s content, which remains the parish’s; the account’s personal data is deleted or anonymised as described in the privacy policy.

sections.title: Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may change these Terms to reflect changes to the service or the law. The update date is shown at the top of the page. For important changes, users will be informed. Continuing to use the service after a change means you accept it.

sections.title: Settling disputes
paragraphs: If there is a problem, contact us first: most disagreements are settled amicably. Failing that, the dispute falls to the courts competent under the law applicable to the publisher of the service. [To be confirmed: applicable law and competent court.]

sections.title: Contact us
paragraphs: For any question about these terms, or to report content, use the Contact page of the site.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Parishes entrust us with information about their worshippers and activities, and we take that trust seriously. This page explains, simply, what data we use, why, who can see it, how long we keep it and how to exercise your rights.

sections.title: Who is responsible for your data?
paragraphs: The data controller is the publisher of the Churchy site, identified in the legal notice. For information a parish publishes on its page (times, parish contact details, announcements), the parish decides what it shares; Churchy then acts as the technical provider that hosts and displays it.
We process your data in line with the personal data protection law applicable in Cameroon and, where it applies, the European regulation (GDPR).

sections.title: Data we collect
paragraphs: We only collect what is useful to the service:
items: Account: last name, first name, email address, password (never stored in clear: only an encrypted fingerprint is kept), chosen language, role(s) in one or more parishes, date the email address was verified.
Use: favourite parishes (on your device if you are not signed in, in your account otherwise); session data (see “Cookies”).
Contact form: name, email, subject and message.
Management content: celebrations, preparation sheets, internal notes, announcements, activities, written by a parish’s members.
Parish public information: the parish’s name, address, city, phone and email, times.
Technical data: IP address, browser type, date and time of requests, error logs, used for security and to limit abuse.
after: We do not ask for a date of birth, photograph, ID number or bank details.

sections.title: A point of care: data touching on religion
paragraphs: Information about religious practice or affiliation is considered sensitive. Having an account linked to a parish, or a parish among your favourites, may reveal some. That is why: we never publish the list of members or favourites; members’ names are only visible in their parish’s management area; a visitor’s favourites stay on their device; we do not sell or hand over any data.

Parishes must not publish worshippers’ data (names, named Mass intentions, health or bereavement information) without their consent. A death notice or a named Mass intention requires the family’s consent.

sections.title: Becoming a follower of a parish
paragraphs: You can become a follower of a parish in one click, with no approval. It is your choice, and you can undo it at any time with “Unfollow”.

The administrators of that parish then see your first name, last name, the date you joined and your status (follower or member). They do not see your email or your phone number. Other followers and members cannot see you.
A parish may recognise you as a member, give you a responsibility (preparing celebrations, reading, announcements) or remove you from its list. When you leave a parish, this information is deleted.

sections.title: What your data is used for
items: Providing the service: creating and securing your account, signing you in, showing the management and public pages (performance of the contract);
Writing to you about the service: confirming your email address, resetting your password, replying to your message (performance of the contract and legitimate interest);
Respecting your language: the interface and emails are sent in French or English as you chose;
Protecting the service: detecting and limiting abuse, intrusion attempts and mass sending (legitimate interest);
Improving the service: fixing errors using technical logs (legitimate interest).
after: We do not use your data for advertising or commercial profiling. We do not send you a newsletter unless you asked for one.

sections.title: Who can see your data?
items: Only you see your password (we cannot access it).
The managers of your parish see your last name, first name, email and role.
A parish’s members see its preparations according to their role; internal notes are reserved for administrators and preparers.
The public sees only what a parish has chosen to publish (announced celebrations, announcements, activities, the parish’s contact details).
Our technical team may access data when needed to keep the service running and secure, under a duty of confidentiality.

sections.title: Providers and hosting
paragraphs: The service is hosted by OVH (see legal notice). Emails go through a mail server that passes them on to your provider. These providers act only on our instructions.
We do not pass your data to advertising networks or data brokers. If a transfer outside your country ever became necessary, we would make sure appropriate safeguards are in place.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: Churchy only uses strictly necessary items: no advertising, no tracking, no third-party analytics. They therefore do not require a consent banner.
items: churchy_at (sign-in, 15 minutes) and churchy_rt (sign-in renewal, 30 days): secure cookies, unreadable by the site’s JavaScript, that keep you signed in;
churchy_session: a simple flag that a session exists, with no personal information;
NEXT_LOCALE (1 year): remembers your chosen language;
Device local storage (churchy:favorites): the favourite parishes of a visitor who is not signed in. It is emptied when you sign in, after being added to your account.
after: You can delete these at any time from your browser settings; you will then need to sign in again and choose your language again.

sections.title: How long do we keep your data?
items: Account: while it is active, then deleted or anonymised within a reasonable time after your deletion request or the account’s closure.
Sessions: renewal tokens expire after 30 days or on sign-out.
Confirmation and reset links: valid for 24 hours and 1 hour, single use.
Contact messages: processed then removed from our sending queue; the copy received by the team is kept as long as needed to reply, then deleted.
Technical logs: kept for a limited time (a few weeks).
A parish’s content: as long as the parish keeps it; it can edit or delete it.

sections.title: How do we protect your data?
paragraphs: Connections use HTTPS; passwords are encrypted with an algorithm designed for that; sessions use protected cookies and automatically renewed tokens; sensitive actions are rate-limited against repeated attacks; each parish is partitioned (a member cannot see another parish’s data); entered text is cleaned to prevent code injection. As no security is absolute, we will inform you, and the competent authority where the law requires, of any data breach that presents a risk.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask at any time for:
items: access to the data about you and a copy;
correction of inaccurate information (you can also edit your details in your area);
deletion of your account and your data;
restriction of processing, or your objection to it for a legitimate reason;
withdrawal of your consent, where processing relies on it.
after: Write to us through the Contact page, stating your account’s email address; we may ask you to confirm your identity. We reply within a reasonable time, at most within one month. If you believe your rights are not respected, you may refer the matter to your country’s data protection authority.

sections.title: Children and minors
paragraphs: The service is aimed at adults serving their community. A minor should only create an account with the consent of their parents or guardian. Parishes must not publish a photograph or information identifying a child without their parents’ permission.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy; the date at the top shows the latest version. For important changes, we will inform you.

sections.title: Contact us
paragraphs: For any question or to exercise your rights, use the Contact page of the site.
